sources.entry: Clipivo - Local-first native clipboard manager that keeps your clipboard history searchable, organized, and private. ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.name: Clipivo
summary.one_liner: Clipivo is a free, local-first native macOS clipboard manager that keeps a searchable, organized history of everything you copy.
use_cases: Find a snippet, link or color you copied earlier
Keep a long-term history of copied text and images
Search text inside screenshots via on-device OCR
Keep work and personal clips separate using Spaces
Paste previously copied items without re-copying them
summary.what_it_does: Clipivo records clipboard contents including text, rich text, images, links, files, code and colors, shown newest first on a panel docked to the bottom of the screen. You can search the history by fragments of text, titles, file names, URLs, text inside images and source app, then click a card or press return to paste it. Clips can be pinned with ⌘P, given titles with ⌘R, and organized into Spaces, where a clip can appear in several Spaces while remaining in History. Image text is recognised on-device with Apple's Vision framework, and apps listed in settings are ignored so their clipboard is never read.
notable: Local-first: no account, no cloud, no uploads or analytics in the default setup
On-device OCR makes screenshot and image text searchable
Ignored apps list skips password managers and chosen apps before reading the clipboard
No item caps; history is paged and Spaces can group clips without moving them
caveats: Free public beta (version 0.9.6-beta); Windows, iPhone/iPad and Android are planned, not available
Source-available under its own license, not open source; on macOS 15+ the first launch needs a Privacy & Security approval because the app lacks a paid Apple certificate
